title: Harness-IF: Evaluating Instruction Following Across Instruction Surfaces in Coding Agents
abstract: arXiv:2608.11727v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When a coding agent obeys a rule, it may simply have been going to do that anyway. Existing instruction-following benchmarks cannot tell the difference: they concentrate rules in the user turn, while coding-agent benchmarks emphasize final task success. We introduce Harness-IF, which scores operational rules one at a time from execution evidence: 60 realistic multi-turn coding items drawn from a 642-rule library, 256 rules receiving verdicts, placed on the five configurable surfaces a deployed agent reads. To separate compliance from coincidence we introduce Against-Prior Accuracy (AP-Acc), which scores only rules labeled as opposing unprompted defaults, observed by re-running tasks with the rule withheld across nine probe builds and curated otherwise. translated_title: Harness-IF：评估编码代理在不同指令面上的指令遵循能力
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.11727v1 公告类型：新 摘要：当编码代理遵守规则时，它可能本来就会这样做。现有的指令遵循基准无法区分这一点：它们将规则集中在用户轮次中，而编码代理基准则强调最终任务成功。我们引入了Harness-IF，它基于执行证据逐条评分操作规则：从642条规则库中提取60个真实的多轮编码项目，256条规则获得裁决，放置在部署代理读取的五个可配置表面上。为了区分遵循与巧合，我们引入了“对抗先验准确性”（AP-Acc），该指标仅对标记为与未提示默认行为相反的规则进行评分，通过在其他九个探针构建中省略规则并重新运行任务来观察。在12个前沿模型中，准确性范围为72.1-85.9%，AP-Acc范围为66.1-78.6%；每个模型在对抗先验规则上的表现都较差，差距为3.6至7.4个百分点（平均5.81），并且这种方向性在通信中得以保持。
tldr: 本文提出Harness-IF基准和AP-Acc指标，用于区分编码代理是否真正遵循指令而非偶然行为，发现所有前沿模型在对抗默认行为的规则上均表现显著较差。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Harness-IF benchmark and AP-Acc metric to distinguish genuine instruction following from coincidental behavior in coding agents, revealing that all frontier models perform significantly worse on rules opposing default behaviors.
